title: Teaming Wisdom Coming from Soccer Field
context_sources: MCM 2020 Problem D: Soccer team performance analysis
Provided passing event data for Huskies team
source_quality: Good OCR quality. 27 pages including 4-page code appendix. Text extraction captures all prose, equations mostly readable. Some table formatting lost in extraction. Watermark present on all pages.

task_reconstruction.official_requirements: MCM 2020 Problem D asks teams to: (1) Build a model capturing performance indicators reflecting successful teamwork in soccer, (2) Evaluate team and opponent performance per match, (3) Analyze strategy effectiveness and provide recommendations, (4) Generalize the model to other teamwork domains.
task_reconstruction.official_context_status: Passing event data provided by MCM organizers for Huskies team across one season.
task_reconstruction.paper_approach: Ball passing network (undirected weighted graph) → network parameters → K-means clustering of dyadic/triadic configurations → Adversarial Regression model (5 indicators, exhaustive weight search) → strategy analysis with formation comparison → generalization to non-sports teamwork.
task_reconstruction.paper_coverage: All four tasks addressed. Task 1: network model with 6 parameters. Task 2: adversarial regression with 5 indicators. Task 3: formation comparison + 3 strategy changes. Task 4: leadership intensity + effective coordination generalization.
coverage_gaps: Generalization purely conceptual without empirical validation
Individual player analysis omitted (acknowledged in weaknesses)

assumptions.summary: The ball passing network is an undirected graph (direction ignored).
Incoming player substitutes outgoing player directly without changing team formation.
Opponent team has equal overall strength to Huskies.
Each player has the same physical quality and individual ability.

models.summary: Undirected weighted graph: nodes=players, edges=passes. Adjacency matrix with 6 network parameters.
K-means clustering on adjacency vectors to identify dyadic and triadic passing subgroups.
Linear regression scoring teamwork via 5 indicators with adversarial constraint on opponent.
Analogy-based extension mapping soccer indicators to general teamwork with leadership and coordination formulas.

contributions.summary: Creative adversarial framing: team score defined relative to opponent, not absolute.
Five interpretable indicators mapping network metrics to tactical concepts.
Exhaustive weight search guaranteeing global optimum within discretized space.
Cross-domain analogy extending soccer model to general teamwork.
Leadership Intensity and Effective Coordination as novel composite indicators.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: MCM-provided passing event data for Huskies team (one season); adjacency matrix constructed from passer-receiver pairs.
Temporal aggregation: 10-minute windows, full match, and season-level.
Spatial aggregation: defensive, midfield, and offensive regions.

verification.summary: Error limit epsilon varied [0,2]; weights stable in [0.5,1.5] range.
Goldilocks comparison: 30-pass too jagged, 70-pass too smooth, 50-pass balanced.

writing_logic.summary: Task-labeled abstract: each competition task previewed in one sentence with Nowadays opener.
Five numbered steps for simulation algorithm; clear procedural structure.
Honest self-assessment listing real weaknesses alongside strengths.

language_observations.summary: Nowadays + increasingly-important-role opener: classic L2 随着 calque.
With-the-development-of opener (随着...的发展 calque) + postposed adverb 'complex increasingly.'
In-a-gesture-to misused for in-an-effort-to (appears twice, pages 9 and 19).
Coined word persuasibility (should be persuasiveness) — morphological over-generalization.
Emotion used for cohesion/chemistry (感情 semantic transfer).

weaknesses.summary: No cross-validation or holdout testing for regression model; overfitting risk with exhaustive fit to training data.
Generalization model entirely conceptual with no empirical validation; reduces credibility of cross-domain claims.
Undirected network loses pass direction information; cannot identify playmakers vs receivers.
K-means K chosen manually without principled selection method.
Single team single season data limits generalizability of regression weights.
Indicator scaling and normalization not described; weight interpretation may be misleading.

independent_extensions.summary: Use directed network to capture pass initiation asymmetry.
Apply elbow method or silhouette analysis for principled K selection.
Add cross-validation or leave-one-match-out validation for regression.
Validate generalization model on non-sports dataset.
Use continuous optimization instead of discrete weight enumeration.

unresolved_questions: How sensitive are results to the undirected assumption?
Would directed network change indicator weights?
Can the 5 indicators generalize to other team sports (basketball, volleyball)?
What is the optimal discretization step for weight search?

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Creative adversarial framing where team score is relative to opponent may have impressed judges as methodologically novel for a D-type problem.
Ambitious generalization to non-sports teamwork demonstrates applied scope, but this is speculative as the extension lacks validation.
Comprehensive multi-scale network analysis (time, region, season) may have shown depth of analysis, but paper alone cannot establish judge reasoning.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Uses five network-derived indicators (Coordination, Distribution, Tempo, Flexibility, Pressing) as multi-dimension evaluation system.
Sensitivity analysis on error limit epsilon plus tempo window goldilocks comparison.
Constructs network from event-level passing data; adjacency matrix as primary data structure.
Four explicit assumptions stated before model building including homogeneity and undirected graph.
